item.title: Unbeaten East Hampton girls soccer seeks first CIAC title: ‘There's definitely pressure'
item.description: East Hampton girls soccer players Ava Ploszay (left) and Liv Correia after the Bellringers won the Shoreline Conference championship 1-0 over Old Saybrook at Valley Regional High School in Deep River Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (Joe Morelli / Hearst Connecticut Media) There is just one CIAC girls soccer tournament team left that has a spotless record: no defeats and no ties. Can you guess without peeking which team that is? If you guessed East Hampton, give yourself a round of applause. The team is currently 17-0-0, having gone through the Shoreline Conference regular season and league tournament unscathed. The Bellringers entered the CIAC tournament ranked No. 1 in the Class M/S coaches poll , which was based on regular-season results, and No. 8 in the GametimeCT power rankings . "We obviously felt like, although we've had a good season, we need to take every game as serious as we possibly can because nobody is just going to hand anything to us," junior midfielder Ava Ploszay said. "If anything, it makes us have a bigger target on our back, so we need to keep performing and take every second as serious as we possibly can." East Hampton will try to extend its streak Tuesday as the top seed in the CIAC Class M tournament against No. 17 Lakeview in a second-round home game at 2 p.m. The perfect record is a byproduct of the cohesive unit the Bellringers have had. As head coach Andrea Giuliano has indicated, this has been building for two seasons. Last year, East Hampton also went through the regular season without a loss, but did have two ties. But you are remembered for how you performed in the postseason. The Bellringers reached the Shoreline Conference final and fell to Valley Regional. They reached the Class M semifinals and lost to eventual champion Foran. A very good season, but not what East Hampton was looking for. "We were really motivated this year to come back," senior forward Liv Correia said. "We were, like, hungry for it (the Shoreline championship). We really wanted it, and we knew that no one was going to give it to us, so we had to come out and work really hard." And East Hampton made it back to the Shoreline final this season. Giuliano said her team "came in with a little bit of a chip on our shoulders this game." The Bellringers pitched their 13th shutout of the season in a 1-0 win against Old Saybrook , earning their first conference crown since 2006. Giuliano called starting center backs Abigail Hambidge and Quinn Rurka two of the team's top players. "They are the reasons why we keep possessions in games more than most teams and I attribute a ton of our defensive success because of them," Giuliano said. "Our goalkeeper in conference went from seeing around 60 saves to only 16." Correia, one of three seniors on the roster, was named the Shoreline Conference Player of the Year. item.title: How Eagles can use their growing collection of premium NFL draft picks
item.description: The Eagles have created options with their draft capital. What they do with those options will determine whether their deadline decisions improve the organization. Following the Jordan Davis agreement, Philadelphia holds five first-round picks and five second-round picks across the next three drafts, according to Jeff McLane’s reported inventory. That matches Adam Schefter’s total of 10 selections in the first two rounds. The collection gives Howie Roseman several paths. None requires announcing a target, predicting a specific draft position, or deciding today how to use every pick. Make multiple selections at premium positions The most direct approach is to draft players. Multiple early selections let Philadelphia address more than one need without relying on later-round prospects to fill immediate openings. The Eagles can evaluate offensive line, defensive line, and other positions based on available talent. Their draft capital should support that evaluation rather than force a predetermined shopping list. Selecting well also creates the possibility of productive players on rookie contracts, helping balance spending elsewhere. Move within a draft when the value supports it Additional selections let Philadelphia move up for a player it values or move down when another team offers worthwhile compensation. That flexibility should not become a trade requirement. Keeping a selection can be the best decision when a strong prospect remains available. The important advantage is having alternatives when the board develops differently than expected. Trade for an established contributor Premium picks can acquire players with an NFL track record. That may become attractive if Philadelphia identifies a specific roster weakness and believes the player’s age, contract, and performance fit its competitive plans. The cost includes more than the pick. An established acquisition can require a substantial contract, limiting the financial advantage of retaining draft choices. Any such move should be tied to a defined need and a realistic assessment of the roster. Spread investment across several years Philadelphia’s early selections are distributed across 2027, 2028, and 2029. That allows the organization to address needs as they evolve rather than concentrating every decision in one offseason. Draft First-round picks Second-round picks 2027 2 1 2028 2 2 2029 1 2 The Eagles do not need to solve every future question with the next available pick. Keep the focus on development Acquiring selections is only part of roster building. Philadelphia must create an environment in which those players can improve, earn responsibilities, and become dependable starters. The Davis trade increased flexibility. It did not guarantee the next successful roster. That will require disciplined decisions, effective coaching, and patience with players whose development will not follow a straight line. item.title: Under-fire Manchester United manager Michael Carrick drives into training at 7.15am with sacking possible TODAY and Mauricio Pochettino leading the race to replace him
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday morning as club chiefs prepare for crunch talks that could see him sacked today. With the Red Devils languishing in the Premier League relegation zone, United States boss Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the frontrunner to take over. Morning arrival precedes crucial talks According to the Daily Mail , Carrick arrived early to train a depleted squad before chief executive Omar Berrada and football director Jason Wilcox hold video talks with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Sunday's 4-4 Aston Villa draw left the 45-year-old with one win in 10 league games, their worst start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago. His exit would mean seeking an eighth permanent boss since 2013. Michael Carrick arrives early to face his fate: Man United manager could be sacked TODAY - as he drives into training ground at 7.15am https://t.co/mVGeWN9LFH — Daily Mail Sport (@MailSport) November 10, 2026 Defiant manager rules out resignation Having replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January, the former midfielder earned a two-year deal in May after losing just two of 17 games to secure third place and Champions League qualification. However, this campaign has unravelled with only two wins across 15 matches in all competitions, coming at home against newly promoted Ipswich Town and Azerbaijan outfit Sabah. Even after surviving a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth last month, a defeat at Chelsea, a midweek European comeback win over Roma and Sunday's draw have failed to ease the pressure. Asked after the Villa clash whether he would consider stepping down, Carrick said : "That's not going to happen. "We're in November. I don't like this situation and where we are. But we can do something about it. I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games." Argentine tactician tops managerial shortlist The report states that 54-year-old Pochettino is now the clear favourite to succeed Carrick and carries a £7 million release clause in his US contract after previously being linked in 2022 and 2024. The former Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea, Southampton and Paris Saint-Germain boss leads a shortlist that also includes Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann , who were both considered after the Bournemouth defeat. Although 48-year-old Howe was previously viewed as the leading candidate, no contact has been made with the ex-Newcastle United manager, who would cost £3m in compensation following his St James' Park exit in July. Meanwhile, Nagelsmann remains unattached after leaving his post with Germany this summer following their World Cup round-of-32 penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay. item.title: Bookmakers Give AS Roma Among the Highest Odds of Winning Serie A
item.description: Bookmakers Give AS Roma Among the Highest Odds of Winning Serie A The 2026/2027 season is still young, but AS Roma fans have plenty to hope for. The club has given supporters plenty of reasons early this season to be optimistic about finishing at the top of the table instead of looking over their shoulders. They are currently unbeaten in their last 10 league games this season, although they’re currently third in the Serie A table. Only Lazio and Inter are ahead of them this season. This AS Roma run of results hasn’t gone unnoticed by the bookies, and they’ve reassessed how they view this season’s Scudetto race. The bookies now favor Roma as one of the leading title challengers, a big shift from the usual talk about them securing a Champions League place in recent seasons. However, if you’ve been betting on football for a long time, you’ll know that good outright odds don’t automatically mean the club has a better chance of winning the league; it just means the bookies see them as having a good chance. What the Serie A Title Odds Actually Say An early November 2026 Serie A title-odds comparison highlights that Inter are at 1.80 odds, with Roma second in the market at 5.50 odds. Juventus are close behind Roma at 8.00 odds, while AC Milan are at 9.00 odds and Como at 13.00 odds. Note that these are only a snapshot of available odds and are not permanent, as odds are volatile. Bookmakers can adjust each team’s odds after one result, an injury, or a change in demand. For a simplified probability calculation, Roma’s 5.50 odds are roughly an 18% chance, while Inter is currently at 56% at 1.80 odds. These figures did not include the bookmaker’s margin, so they should not be treated as objective forecasts. However, they explain the market’s message. Roma have moved into serious contention and title conversation, even though Inter remain the favourites. Interest in Italian football extends far beyond the peninsula. For example, an Asian sports platform, GemBet , includes Serie A among the European competitions covered in its sports sections. This shows the league’s international audience and appeal. Why Roma Have Become Credible Contenders The Serie A league table provides a stronger insight than any headline about betting odds. According to AS Roma’s official standings , they have seven wins, three draws, and haven’t lost any of their first 10 matches in the league. More impressively, AS Roma have scored 28 goals and conceded just ten, and this gives them a goal difference of plus 18. The current AS record becomes more impressive when you check the two teams above them on the Serie A table. Gian Piero Gasperini’s side have scored more goals than the two teams above them on the table, despite sitting four points behind Lazio and one behind Inter. item.title: Laura Stegall taught her daughter to play volleyball - and a lot more about how to fight
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS — Laura Stegall is somewhere amid the sea of blue that's overtaken half the lower bowl at Gainbridge Fieldhouse Saturday night. She's sporting blue-and-white checkered overalls, celebrating the now three-time defending Class 4A state champion Fort Wayne Carroll volleyball team's four-set win over Center Grove with her son, Brady. Down on the floor, Laura's daughters — senior outside hitter Sarah and freshman setter Ashtyn — are posing for a photo with their dad, Carroll assistant athletic director Randy Stegall. Sarah credits both her parents with "setting the standard" in her life. But her love for volleyball was inspired by Laura, who was a two-sport athlete at Indiana Purdue Fort Wayne (basketball), then launched college volleyball programs at Indiana Tech and Daytona State (Fla.). Laura was Sarah's first coach, the one who taught the Notre Dame commit everything she knows. The two text about the sport on a near-daily basis, Sarah says. "She gets a message before every game, whether she wants it or not," Laura adds in a separate interview. My mom wants the best for me, to make sure I'm always playing with confidence, Sarah explains from outside Gainbridge, the blue championship medal draped around her neck and Laura standing proudly alongside her. The odds were stacked against Laura living to see her oldest child reach high school, let alone play out her senior season. Laura was diagnosed with late-stage ovarian cancer in February 2019. She was given a 39% chance of living five years and a 20% of making it a decade. "But by the grace of God, I'm here eight years later," Laura said in a phone interview with IndyStar last week. Sarah was her family's bedrock while her mother underwent cancer treatments. Just nine years old at the time, she took charge at home, cooking meals and looking after her siblings so Laura could rest while Randy, a college baseball coach at the time, was on the road. "Sarah's truly one of the most responsible, mature people and she stepped up so majorly for our family," Laura says before being overwhelmed by her emotions. "That's a lot to ask of a 9-year-old: 'Hey, I need you to do this for your brother. I need you to cook dinner,' but Sarah stepped up — and she still cooks better than me." Laura takes a moment to collect herself, then reflects on one of her favorite sports memories with Sarah, a swim meet back when the family still lived in Florida. Laura had recently completed cancer treatments and was in attendance to see her 10-year old daughter break a 28-year old breaststroke record. It was a "euphoric moment," she says, her pride beaming through the phone. "And every little benchmark along the way. … I'm sitting there watching Sarah like, 'I'm so grateful to be here to see this.'" 'Mom, are you gonna die?' Sarah remembers basically everything from that day in 2019. It was 5:30 p.m. and the 9-year-old still was still at school. item.description: Motorsport photo Aprilia Racing CEO Massimo Rivola insists his team didn't lose the 2026 MotoGP title, but that Marc Marquez won it through his outstanding performances on the Ducati. Marquez is on the verge of securing his 10th motorcycle racing world title and his eighth in the MotoGP category. He had his first 'match point' to clinch the championship in Qatar, though he always knew his chances were slim last weekend. The Spaniard won Saturday’s sprint race in Losail, and on Sunday – secured a valuable second-place finish. He could now be crowned champion next Saturday in Portimao by winning the sprint race. The Ducati rider simply needs to outscore Jorge Martin by two points, while a top-nine finish would definitively eliminate the threat from Marco Bezzecchi , who is 74 points adrift, with exactly 74 points still remaining to be scored. Given the nature of the season and the dynamics observed across the 20 grands prix held so far, a debate has emerged among fans and within the paddock in recent weeks: has Marquez won the title (pending, of course, its official confirmation), or has Aprilia lost it? Following the Qatar GP, Aprilia CEO Massimo Rivola was asked who is most responsible for the season's final outcome. In an interview with Sky Sport, the Italian praised Marquez's performance, while expressing regret that his own factory - despite delivering its best-ever season in the premier class - has been unable to secure the riders' championship. When asked whether Marquez won the title or Aprilia lost it, Rivola replied: "Marc Marquez won it. Honestly, he was the deciding factor. He proved it again in this Sunday’s race; just look at the gap between him and the other Ducatis. "The way he managed his race weekends, the way he racked up 37 points whenever the opportunity arose, and the way he navigated the most challenging circuits. I take my hat off to him. I admire his track record, his experience, and even the way he handles the press. Nothing happens by chance; Marc is truly a great." item.title: “This Is Worse Than Brandon Staley”: NFL Analyst Claims Chargers Players Have Quit on Jim Harbaugh Amid 0–8 Start
item.description: Jim Harbaugh © Imagn. The Los Angeles Chargers remain winless after eight games as questions grow around head coach Jim Harbaugh. The Chargers lost to the Houston Texans, 44-22, last week, extending their losing streak to 11 games and dropping to 0-8. NFL analyst John Middlekauff claimed that Harbaugh has lost the locker room’s confidence after last week’s humiliating loss. On his podcast 3 & OUT with John Middlekauff , the analyst compared Harbaugh with former Chargers head coach Brandon Staley, who was fired in his third season. “1, 2, 3, trade me, please. 1, 2, 3, we quit. 1, 2, 3, this is worse than Brandon Staley,” Middlekauff said. “If Jim Harbaugh’s name was Jim Middlekauff, I think he probably would’ve already been fired. And he definitely might get fired after this game. But he’s Jim Harbaugh. And his resume is really impressive. And he makes a ton of money… You can blame Mike McDaniel. Like, this feels bigger than him. This feels, like, organizationally, you know, as Jim lost it, which is crazy to say, but it feels like overnight, like he got no pulse on his team and they’ve quit on him.” Given everything that has unraveled this season for the Chargers, Middlekauff is not sure about any player ahead of the trade deadline. “I know they’ve been adamant, we’re not trading anybody. We’re not trading Khalil Mack,” Middlekauff added. “I’d even say, like, I’d be stunned if they trade Herbert. At this point in time, the next couple of days with the Chargers, nothing will shock me. Nothing.” The locker room frustration came to the fore after Chargers tight end Charlie Kolar offered insight into his own mindset. Following the loss against the Texans, the tight end admitted that at 0–8 it’s difficult to remain “mentally and emotionally present.” Jim Harbaugh Pushes Back Against Questions About Players’ Commitment After Sunday’s game, questions were raised about whether the Chargers players have already given up on the season. Jim Harbaugh strongly rejected the notion during Monday’s press conference. “Just about everybody on our team, most of the guys, they’ve been part of the winning,” Harbaugh said via the Chargers’ website . “A lot of winning. Keep fighting. There’s fighting, or there’s slunking away. That will never be a part of our culture, our organization, any narrative that we’re not hellbent on winning these games is completely wrong.” With the season reaching the halfway point, the Chargers’ next opportunity to win their first game this season will come against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night. item.title: NBA fans in Texas could attend Monday’s Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks games for less than $15
item.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Over the years, there have been a lot of complaints about the rising cost of attending an NBA game, but fans in Texas were offered incredible get-in prices for Monday’s slate of games. With three NBA teams, Texas is the state that boasts the second-most franchises, only behind California with four. All three teams have exciting, big-name superstars and playoff aspirations. But you would never know that, going by the ticket prices they were charging for games on Monday night. Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks had incredibly low get-in prices for Monday night games According to data from TickPick , the Houston Rockets vs. Denver Nuggets had a staggeringly low get-in price of just $10 hours before tip-off. As for the Dallas Mavericks, who hosted the Indiana Pacers (albeit without Tyrese Haliburton), they offered fans a get-in price of just $14. These get-in ticket prices actually cost less than the average cost of a six-wing meal combo at WingStop, which only goes to show how affordable the deal was for fans. And while going through first- or third-party ticketing platforms would have added some fees to the overall price of the order, NBA fans in Texas would still be getting a very good deal given the average price of NBA tickets elsewhere in the country and the superstars that were playing. The get-in price of the Rockets vs. Nuggets game is especially surprising, as it boasted two all-time great superstars in Nikola Jokic and Kevin Durant. With a superstar pairing that boasts four MVPs, three NBA championships, and three Finals MVPs between them, you would imagine the demand for tickets would be much higher. And on top of that, both teams are seen as possible contenders, with the Rockets currently on one of their best starts to an NBA season in recent memory. As for the Dallas Mavericks, while they were playing an Indiana Pacers team that is heavily depleted following the loss of Tyrese Haliburton due to injury, their own star pairing of Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg should have been enough to demand a higher get-in price for their game on Monday night. Fans that grabbed tickets at these low prices will be grateful, as it is unlikely that such star-studded teams will get to play again at such a low price again this season.
